newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia housing data in line with pickup - govt.
newsitem.headline: Australia housing data in line with pickup - govt.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Friday housing finance data released earlier on Friday was consistent with an industry pick-up.
He also repeated that the lastest cut in official interests had still to feed through into the economy.

"We've always said throughout the course of 1997 we expect the housing market to turn up, that really what we had was a supply problem on the housing market and as supply and demand got back into an equilibrium you'd see the market pick up and these figures are consistent with that," Costello told reporters.

Asked about interest rates, Costello said: "We've had an interest rate reduction pretty recently and I think we're still to see some of the banks pass it on in full, so we'd be happy if the banks passed that on in full to the standard mortgage before anybody starts calling for future action."
Figures released earlier on Friday showed Australia housing finance by volume fell 8.4 percent in May, seasonally adjusted.
Speculation has risen in financial markets that the Reserve Bank will soon cut official cash interest rates from their current 5.5 percent after Thursday's weaker than expected employment data.
"My point to you is not what's going to happen in the future, let's look what's happening at the moment and what's happening at the moment is we have a lower interest rate climate," Costello said.
The Reserve Bank has eased monetary policy four times in less than a year, reducing rates by 0.5 percentage points each time.
The latest rate cut was on May 23, while the first was in July last year.
